# Feasibility, architecture and correlated allocations {#sec-feasibility-allocations}

A receiver can have enough gain, a precise phase estimate and a fast data link,
yet still fail its task. The gain may clip the blocker, the phase may select the
wrong spatial branch, or the estimate may arrive after the scene has changed.
Architecture selection starts by intersecting these conditions at the same
operating point. A favorable calculation in each of several incompatible states
is not a feasible receiver.

This bounded development asks whether a small direction-comparison receiver can
meet a supplied angular, blocker and response-time brief. The reader should be
able to turn a need into a conditioned observable, calculate incompatible gain
and information constraints, compare interface/resource alternatives, and state
which missing evidence prevents a hardware recommendation. We then refine the
initial interfaces into physical correlated allocations and test budget closure. Requirement framing
begins in [Chapter 1](phase-comparison.qmd#sec-requirement-framing). We use
[Chapter 5](phase-delay-inference.qmd) to separate precision from ambiguity,
[Chapter 6](model-adequacy-uncertainty.qmd) to qualify approximations, and
[Chapters 8–10](fields-geometry-transduction.qmd) for field, disturbance and
extraction interfaces. [Chapter 11](frequency-phase-delay-transfer.qmd) fixes
conversion orientation, reference signs and sample-state prerequisites before
those interfaces are allocated. Numerical envelopes below are **synthetic design inputs**,
not selected products or measured receiver performance.

## Joint feasible regions {#sec-joint-feasibility}

### A brief that can fail

Suppose one far-field, linearly polarized narrowband source near 1 GHz is to be
located within a known front sector $|\theta|\leq60^\circ$. The observable is
source direction relative to the array normal at the record midpoint, inferred
from simultaneous, orientation-normalized channel voltages. A single plane-wave
manifold is supplied; multipath, unknown polarization and installation errors
must eventually be tested rather than included by assertion. Use rounded
propagation speed $3.00\times10^8$ m/s, hence wavelength $\lambda=0.300$ m.
The following is an illustrative operational brief, not a project requirement.

| Condition or limit | Supplied value and meaning |
|---|---|
| Wanted input and blocker at RF ports P0 | Wanted tone near 1.000 GHz, −100 dBm/channel; one CW blocker near 1.010 GHz, −20 dBm/channel; each tuning-offset uncertainty at most 100 Hz |
| Angular task | Local standard uncertainty at most 0.5° near the sector edge, conditional on the correct branch; branch-error probability at most $10^{-3}$; blocker-induced angular bias at most 0.02° |
| Time and dynamics | Report within 5 ms of record start; post-record processing/transfer 0.6 ms; angular excursion during a constant-manifold record at most 0.05°, with supplied rate bound 20°/s |
| Residual carrier offset | At most 100 Hz after supplied coarse tuning; no claim that a shared clock removes it |
| Noise/energy interface | Per-channel coherent tone SNR $\rho=100$ in 1 ms at zero offset after the selected front end; independent proper Gaussian channel noise, fixed phase and no fades |
| Digitizer interface P2 | Weak-tone floor −60 dBm; maximum composite peak voltage 0.100 V into an effective 50 Ω, equivalent to −10 dBm CW power; both are supplied qualified-interface limits |
| Complete observation interface | Desired positive-frequency component retained and orientation normalized; sum of magnitudes of all blocker-to-record image/alias paths, including conversion/filtering and the finite record, at most $10^{-5}$ of the wanted response |
| Resources | Total receiver 2.5 W; sustained link 5 Gbit/s including framing; three simultaneous channels allowed |

The specified noise SNR is after the complete observation in the selected 46 dB
gain state; another gain/filter state needs its own input-referred noise and
observation-noise gain. The noise interface can equivalently specify a wanted power −102 dBm at the
preselector output P1 and an effective power density −152 dBm/Hz there. Their
ratio is $C/N_0=10^5$ Hz and the ideal coherent tone observation gives
$\rho=(C/N_0)T$. That density must include the actual filter, amplifier and
converter-referred contributions; a passive insertion loss is not noiseless.
The stated density is an input requiring evidence, not a derivation from the
blocker level or a nominal noise figure. Chapter 9 constructs such contributions.

The weak-tone floor at P2 is likewise a supplied interface contract. Fourteen
stored bits below will set link traffic, **not** establish this floor or effective
resolution. Kester's [MT-001](https://www.analog.com/media/en/training-seminars/tutorials/MT-001.pdf),
Rev. A, p. 1, identifies the ideal converter and decorrelation assumptions behind
its quantization-noise model. It supplies no guarantee for the proposed blocker
and weak-tone combination. Driver loading, overload recovery, actual noise and
spurs remain implementation evidence needs.

For architecture variables $\mathbf x$ and environmental/state inputs
$\boldsymbol\eta$, write the conditional feasible set as

$$
 \mathcal F(\boldsymbol\eta)=
 \{\mathbf x:g_r(\mathbf x,\boldsymbol\eta)\leq0\ \text{for every required }r\}.
$$

An empty set rejects that combination of requirements, assumptions and available
alternatives. A nonempty model set is **conditional** until its technology,
physical inputs and task mapping are supported. If $\boldsymbol\eta$ lies in a
justified bounded set $\mathcal E$, robustness means satisfying the constraints
for every $\boldsymbol\eta\in\mathcal E$; choosing the most favorable unknown
value proves only existence of an optimistic case. An unspecified nuisance
cannot be silently assigned zero.

For a fixed architecture this distinction is $\exists\mathbf x\,
\forall\boldsymbol\eta\in\mathcal E$, not
$\forall\boldsymbol\eta\,\exists\mathbf x$. An adaptive architecture must
include its allowed sensing, state changes, latency and policies among the design
variables before claiming that it handles different conditions.

### Gain does not create headroom

First intersect weak-tone visibility and composite-input survival. Let $G$ be
the conversion/voltage-chain **power gain in dB** between equal 50 Ω reference
planes, $L_s$ the wanted insertion loss, and $A_B$ the blocker's total RF
attenuation in dB. At the gain input, powers in milliwatts are

$$
 p_s=10^{(-100-L_s)/10},\qquad p_b=10^{(-20-A_B)/10}.
$$

With worst relative tone phase, the peak voltage is proportional to
$\sqrt{p_s}+\sqrt{p_b}$. Thus the equivalent composite peak power before gain is
$p_{\rm pk}=(\sqrt{p_s}+\sqrt{p_b})^2$, and the two bounds are

$$
 G_{\min}=-60-(-100-L_s)=40+L_s,\qquad
 G_{\max}=-10-10\log_{10}p_{\rm pk}.
$$

This is a peak constraint, not an incoherent addition of average powers. For
more carriers replace the two amplitudes by a justified envelope or crest-factor
bound. Gain must exist in $[G_{\min},G_{\max}]$ and every intermediate stage must
also survive the waveform. Final-output headroom alone cannot establish that.

With no preselection, $L_s=A_B=0$: the bounds are 40 and 9.99913 dB. Their
intersection is empty by approximately 30 dB. A digital blocker notch after
sampling cannot restore clipped information. Now supply a selector family with
$L_s=2$ dB, and choose $A_B=40$ dB. The bounds become 42 and 49.93128 dB.
At $G=46$ dB, wanted and blocker powers at P2 are −56 and −14 dBm; the
worst composite is −13.93128 dBm, within the supplied −10 dBm limit.
The gain interval is now nonempty, conditional on linearity and noise evidence.

@fig-gain-feasibility shows how attenuation creates an interval rather than
merely changing a nominal operating point. Reducing $A_B$ to 30 dB while retaining
2 dB wanted loss leaves $G_{\max}\simeq39.98$ dB, still below 42 dB.
The architecture needs attenuation at the correct plane, not a larger gain
number or a cleaner output after clipping. The simplified first-stage input
survival envelope is −15 dBm; the selected branch sees a −60 dBm blocker, but
an actual stage-by-stage gain/drive allocation is still required.

### Information, ambiguity and available time

A baseline $d$ along the array axis has relative field phase
$\phi=kd\sin\theta$, where $k=2\pi/\lambda$, using Chapter 8's sourceward
geometry and Chapter 1's normalized orientation. A phase report is modulo $2\pi$.
To avoid two noiseless directions in the closed sector sharing the same phase,
require

$$
 2kd\sin60^\circ<2\pi,\qquad
 d<d_{\rm amb}={\lambda\over2\sin60^\circ}=0.173205\ \mathrm m.
$$

The inequality is strict: equality aliases the two sector endpoints. This is a
single-baseline, single-frequency result under the supplied manifold, not a
universal aperture limit.

For a sufficiently strong tone with proper Gaussian complex noise, Chapter 2's
small-noise phase approximation gives per-channel phase variance $1/(2\rho)$.
Independent equal-noise channels therefore have relative-phase variance
$1/\rho$. Linearizing the phase-angle relation gives

$$
 \sigma_\theta\simeq{1\over kd|\cos\theta|\sqrt\rho},\qquad
 d\geq d_{\rm prec}={1\over k|\cos\theta|\sigma_{\theta,\max}\sqrt\rho}.
$$

Use radians in this calculation. At the edge approached from inside the sector,
$|\cos\theta|=1/2$, $\sigma_{\theta,\max}=0.00872665$ rad and $\rho=100$:
$d_{\rm prec}=1.094269$ m. There is no baseline satisfying both 1.094269 m
minimum precision aperture and 0.173205 m maximum unambiguous baseline. A local
precision calculation alone would have selected a globally ambiguous design.
The linearized uncertainty is conditional on the correct branch; it is not a
Gaussian model for arbitrarily large angle errors or an edge-clipped estimator.

Increasing gain does not improve this input-referred SNR when signal and dominant
analog noise are amplified together. Increasing observation time can improve
energy, but the time must exist. For a normalized rectangular tone observation
with residual frequency $\delta f$, direct integration of
$T^{-1}\int_0^T e^{j2\pi\delta f t}dt$ gives amplitude
$e^{j\pi\delta fT}\operatorname{sinc}(\delta fT)$, with
$\operatorname{sinc}x=\sin(\pi x)/(\pi x)$. Consequently

$$
 \rho(T,\delta f)=(10^5\,\mathrm{Hz})T\operatorname{sinc}^2(\delta fT).
$$

This is an explicit observation model, not a universal integration-loss rule.
The constant-manifold excursion requirement gives $T\leq0.05/20=2.5$ ms;
latency alone gives $T\leq4.4$ ms. Thus 2.5 ms is the tighter supplied limit.
A short baseline $d_s=0.150$ m would need $\rho=5321.885$ even before other
errors: 53.21885 ms at zero offset. It cannot obtain that energy within the
brief. At 100 Hz residual offset and 1 ms, $\rho=96.75312$ rather than 100.
Both the wanted response and noise normalization must follow the observation.

@fig-aperture-feasibility makes the precision/ambiguity conflict visible.
A 1.2 m baseline meets the local 0.5° target at 1 ms, but its wrapped phase
cannot select the correct direction. A 0.15 m baseline resolves the sector but
cannot meet that precision with the available energy. More information, a

restricted sector, a changed deadline/energy envelope or another measured
observable is needed.

Short and long baselines provide different information rather than interchangeable gain.](figures/aperture-feasibility.svg){#fig-aperture-feasibility fig-alt="Minimum aperture for0.5degree local uncertainty near60degrees versus coherent SNR, with a horizontal0.1732m ambiguity ceiling and candidate0.15m and1.2m baselines. ## Architecture and quantitative interfaces {#sec-architecture-interfaces}

Consider three simultaneous ports at positions 0, 0.15 and 1.20 m. The long
baseline supplies local precision, while the short baseline supplies a coarse
sector estimate. This is a bounded ambiguity-restoration example, not a complete
bearing estimator or a claim that three elements solve multipath/polarization.
The source amplitude/common phase is a nuisance removed by relative comparisons.
A single analog-combined complex output cannot generally recover direction from
one unknown complex source amplitude: for any nonzero combined response $b(u)$,
its change can be absorbed into that amplitude. Multiple independent beam outputs
or scans can restore information, but their timing and manifold must be budgeted.
Analog reception is a valid alternative when those interfaces are supplied.

For the selected simultaneous case let $u=\sin\theta$ and
$\Delta u=\lambda/d_l=0.25$ be long-baseline branch spacing. Fine candidates
come from adding integer cycles to its phase; select the one nearest the short
baseline's direction cosine. Ignoring channel-noise correlation would misstate
that decision's uncertainty: both differences contain the reference channel.
If individual small phase errors $\epsilon_0,\epsilon_s,\epsilon_l$ are
independent with variance $1/(2\rho)$, the branch-comparison error is

$$
 e_u={\epsilon_s-\epsilon_0\over kd_s}
       -{\epsilon_l-\epsilon_0\over kd_l},\qquad
 \sigma_{e_u}^2={1\over\rho}
 \left[{1\over(kd_s)^2}+{1\over(kd_l)^2}-{1\over(kd_s)(kd_l)}\right].
$$

The cross term follows from the shared $\epsilon_0$ source; it is not an arbitrary
correlation coefficient. In the high-SNR Gaussian phase approximation,
$2\Phi[-\Delta u/(2\sigma_{e_u})]$ bounds a nearest-branch error when the coarse
phase has not wrapped, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. To avoid treating
that qualification as automatic, add a coarse-wrap bound. The minimum distance
to its principal-phase boundary over the sector is
$m=\pi-kd_s\sin60^\circ$. A conservative union bound is

$$
 P_{\rm branch}\ \lesssim\
 2\Phi\!\left(-{\Delta u\over2\sigma_{e_u}}\right)
 +2\Phi(-m\sqrt\rho).
$$

The approximate sign recalls the linear Gaussian phase model, not a measured
error rate. At 1 ms and worst 100 Hz residual offset, the two terms are
$4.258\times10^{-5}$ and $3.472\times10^{-5}$, totaling less than
$7.74\times10^{-5}$, below the supplied $10^{-3}$ limit. The long-baseline
local uncertainty is approximately 0.46353°. No calibration, multipath or state
error has yet been charged; the apparent margin is not available twice.
A branch failure is a large error event, not another small term to RSS into 0.46353°.

### The blocker must also pass through the observation

The preceding numbers omit retained blocker contamination. Headroom alone does
not justify that omission. After the RF selector the blocker is 42 dB above the
wanted tone, an amplitude ratio $R_B=10^{42/20}=125.8925$. For example, if a
changed operating condition placed it 100.5 kHz from the wanted tone and no
additional rejection were supplied, a 1 ms rectangular observation would retain
$R_B|\operatorname{sinc}(100.5)|=0.39873$ times the wanted amplitude. That can
change the phase and even the selected spatial branch without clipping.
Receiver passband width is not a statement of stopband rejection.

The brief therefore specifies the **composite** observation amplitude ratio
$\eta_B\leq10^{-5}$ at the allowed 1.010 GHz blocker frequencies, relative to
the wanted response. This −100 dB amplitude-transfer specification bounds the sum of path magnitudes for both
real-signal images and any aliased route into the reported record; it is not
merely a digital-filter attenuation at one nominal frequency. The 200 kHz IF
width below is a receiver passband, not an assumed arbitrary modulated waveform.
The calculation here remains a tone comparison. A real implementation must
demonstrate this rejection across frequency/state while preserving the assumed
wanted gain and the full observation noise SNR. Its filtering/digital extraction
is included in the supplied 0.6 ms processing and power envelopes; whether a
specific implementation meets all of them remains unknown.

With that contract, normalize each wanted record mean to a unit phasor. The
retained blocker phasor has magnitude at most
$r=R_B\eta_B=0.00125893$. A circle of radius $r<1$ about the wanted phasor has
maximum phase departure $\beta=\sin^{-1}r$ (the ray tangent to that circle).
Its minimum amplitude is $1-r$. Thus the long-baseline phase bias is bounded
by $2\beta$, corresponding to approximately 0.01149° angle bias near 60°,
below the separate 0.02° blocker allocation. Use the actual inverse sine of
the perturbed direction cosine if a local angle approximation is inadequate.

For a conservative high-SNR noise calculation use
$\rho_{\min}=\rho(1-r)^2=96.50966$, giving local uncertainty about 0.46412°.
Let $\sigma_{e_u,{\rm wc}}$ denote the earlier error SD calculated using this
reduced SNR, and bound the branch-comparison mean displacement by
$b_u=2\beta[1/(kd_s)+1/(kd_l)]$. Subtract these bias allowances from the
decision margins before computing tails:

$$
 P_{\rm branch}\ \lesssim\
 2\Phi\!\left(-{\Delta u/2-b_u\over\sigma_{e_u,{\rm wc}}}\right)
 +2\Phi[-(m-2\beta)\sqrt{\rho_{\min}}]
 <8.90\times10^{-5}.
$$

This requires positive margins and retains the Gaussian phase approximation;
it is a conditional model bound, not an empirical error rate. The conservative
baseline bias bounds do not assume independent blocker phases. @fig-blocker-observation shows why RF survival and retained interference are
separate constraints. Other reference, calibration, environmental and manifold
errors remain to be allocated. If the
composite rejection is unavailable, the candidate's information closure remains
open even though its headroom interval is nonempty.

## Correlated budget construction {#sec-correlated-budget}

The 1 ms candidate has survived an initial feasibility screen. Can it still meet
0.5° once physical shared sources, calibration and environmental departures are
charged? We now refine its supplied interfaces. The reader should be able to
construct a source-to-observable budget, calculate a correlated allocation,
identify an unknown input that prevents closure, and choose a restoring change.
This is a local comparison in a known steady state, not a complete direction
finder or a production distribution. The initial table's independent channel-noise
assumption is now replaced by a common-source model at the same marginal density.
Earlier independent-noise precision/branch numbers remain first-pass calculations,
not results for this revised model.

[Chapter 11](frequency-phase-delay-transfer.qmd) supplies the conversion signs;
[Chapter 9](physical-disturbance-paths.qmd) supplies source/network and reciprocal
mixing models. We reuse [Chapter 4](covariance-quadratic-forms.qmd)'s source-root
covariance and [Chapter 6](model-adequacy-uncertainty.qmd)'s local uncertainty
propagation rather than introduce another uncertainty convention. For this
calculation, interpret the 0.5° criterion as **predictive local standard
uncertainty given the calibration information and declared unobserved environment**,
on a correct spatial branch. Holding an actual temperature and calibration error
fixed gives a different repeated-record variance. Neither interpretation is an

all-error or coverage guarantee.

Let $\boldsymbol\varphi=[\phi_s-\phi_0,\phi_l-\phi_0]^T$ be restored relative
phases at the record midpoint. If $\mathbf e=[e_0,e_s,e_l]^T$ is a vector of small
channel phase errors, define

$$
\mathbf D=\begin{bmatrix}-1&1&0\\-1&0&1\end{bmatrix},\qquad
\delta\boldsymbol\varphi=\mathbf D\mathbf e.
$$

A physical source reaching several ports contributes one column, or one filtered
source process, before the covariance is formed. For centered stationary phase
sources with two-sided matrix $\mathbf S_q(f)$, ordered as $Q_iQ_j^*$ in
rad²/Hz, let $\mathbf L(f)$ map those sources into channel phase and let
$\mathbf G(f)$ represent the declared normalized phase observation. The finite
output covariance is the corresponding quadratic spectral integral over all
real $f$, where it converges. For a task row $\mathbf w$ acting on the channel
phases, its variance contribution is

$$
 V_{\mathbf w}=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
 [\mathbf w\mathbf G(f)\mathbf L(f)]\mathbf S_q(f)
 [\mathbf w\mathbf G(f)\mathbf L(f)]^H\,df.
$$ {#eq-budget-spectral}

This is a use of the existing observation/covariance results. It is not generally
an unweighted integral of a connector phase-noise plot. For example, for a
centered rectangular complex-tone record with common residual offset $\delta$,
linearizing the phase of its complex average gives the real even time weight
$g_\delta(t)=\cos(2\pi\delta t)/[T\operatorname{sinc}(\delta T)]$ inside
$[-T/2,T/2]$, provided the denominator is nonzero. Its integral is one: writing $Z_0=A\operatorname{sinc}(\delta T)$ and
$\delta Z=jA T^{-1}\int e^{j2\pi\delta t}\psi(t)dt$ for a small real phase
perturbation gives $\delta\arg Z=\operatorname{Im}(\delta Z/Z_0)=\int g_\delta(t)\psi(t)dt$.
Use its
Fourier transform for the phase observation, together with the actual path
response; the weight becomes uniform only at zero offset. Additive voltage and
clock/blocker products require their own linearized transfers. A scalar phase
weight cannot replace Chapter 9's complete-waveform timing model.

### Allocate the complete noise floor once

The supplied $N_0=-152$ dBm/Hz at P1 equals
$6.30957\times10^{-19}$ W/Hz in the power-normalized positive-carrier envelope.
It already represents the complete selected observer's effective input-referred
noise. A possible **synthetic partition** is matched thermal input $k_B(290\text{ K})$,
converter-referred contribution $0.4N_0$, common reciprocal-mixing contribution
$qN_0$, and remaining independent active-path contribution
$(0.6-q)N_0-k_B(290\text{ K})$. At $q=0.02$, these are all nonnegative and sum
to $N_0$. The thermal term is $4.00388\times10^{-21}$ W/Hz. It could describe
independent matched source terminations and isothermal passive selectors; an
actual antenna environment/coupled network needs the field/noise model of
Chapter 9 instead. Active-device voltage/current noise and converter noise must
be transferred to P1 through their actual noise gains before using these entries.
This partition demonstrates an admissible source model, not measured noise,
actual component feasibility or an inference from nominal resolution.

For the selected blocker power $P_B=10^{-9}$ W at P1, Chapter 9's narrow-blocker,
flat-effective-spectrum limit gives $N_{\rm rm}=P_B S_{\phi,\rm eff}(-\Delta)$,
$\Delta=10$ MHz in the restored orientation. Allocating $q=0.02$ requires an
effective **two-sided phase density** about $1.26191\times10^{-11}$ rad²/Hz there,
with the appropriate finite-observation weighting. No universal conversion to
one-sided $L(f)$ is being adopted. Spectral shape, internal LO branches and
band limits must be known to replace that flat-spectrum interface by an integral.
A notch rejecting the blocker tone does not remove reciprocal noise that has
already landed in the wanted band.

The [examined mixer-noise article](https://www.analog.com/en/resources/technical-articles/specifications-and-measurement-of-local-oscillator-noise-in-integrated-circuit-base-station-mixers.html),
“Mixer Noise Model” and “Effective Noise Floor of LO Driver,” distinguishes
blocked from ordinary noise-figure conditions and includes internal driver noise.

Adding $qN_0$ to the already complete $N_0$ would double count it. If an earlier
floor was actually measured **without** the blocker, it was a different interface:
recompute the total, SNR and covariance rather than relabel the same number.

Equal marginal channel SNRs still do not supply their covariance. In a simplified
common-LO model after the complete observation, write normalized voltage noise

$$
 n_i=\rho^{-1/2}\{\sqrt{1-q}\,\eta_i+\sqrt q\,v_i\eta_B\},

The $\eta_i$ and $\eta_B$ are mutually independent proper complex Gaussian
variables; $\eta_B$ is one selected LO-noise band translated by the blocker, not

identical relative electronic responses at wanted and blocker frequencies and

requiring suitable sideband selection; significant improper or finite-image noise

integral, not merely the diagonal SNR. Linearizing phase at a unit mean gives
$\epsilon_i=\operatorname{Im}n_i$. Proper centered noise satisfies
$E[\operatorname{Im}n_i\operatorname{Im}n_j]=\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}E[n_i n_j^*]$, giving

$$
\mathbf C_{\varphi,n}=\frac1{2\rho}\mathbf D
 \{(1-q)\mathbf I+q\operatorname{Re}(\mathbf v\mathbf v^H)\}\mathbf D^T.
$$ {#eq-blocker-phase-covariance}

The off-diagonal entries are derived from the single physical source. In
particular the long comparison's variance is
$(1-q\cos\psi_l)/\rho$, where $\psi_l=\arg(v_l v_0^*)$.
A common source cancels only with the relevant equal complex sensitivities.

1	# Frequency, phase and delay transfer {#sec-transfer-plan}
     2	
     3	A frequency plan can put every carrier in the intended band and still reverse a
     4	bearing, conjugate a modulation or change phase at each restart. The engineering
     5	question here is more specific: **what complex waveform does a declared RF input
     6	produce at the comparison record, in each identified state?** A useful answer is
     7	an annotated transfer law, with unwanted paths and validity conditions alongside
     8	it. A list of center frequencies is insufficient.

    12	$v_R(t)=\operatorname{Re}\{a(t)e^{j2\pi f_Rt}\}$ and channel $i$ relative to
    13	reference channel 0 means $\arg(z_i z_0^*)$. The Fourier kernel is
    14	$e^{-j2\pi ft}$. These remain local declared conventions, not new book-wide

    27	## Conversion and reference signs {#sec-conversion-signs}
    28	
    29	Let the LO at mixer plane L be $2\cos(2\pi f_Lt+\lambda)$. The factor 2 simply
    30	normalizes this ideal mathematical multiplier to unit difference-band voltage
    31	gain; actual conversion gain has units, loading and drive conditions. Expand the
    32	real RF signal as one half of an analytic component plus its conjugate. The
    33	product contains components at $\pm(f_R+f_L)$ and $\pm(f_R-f_L)$.
    34	Selecting the **positive-frequency difference band**, with nonoverlapping bands,
    35	gives the following envelopes:
    36	
    37	$$
    38	b(t)=\begin{cases}
    39	 a(t)e^{-j\lambda},& f_R>f_L,\\
    40	 a^*(t)e^{j\lambda},& f_L>f_R.
    41	\end{cases}
    42	$$ {#eq-mixer-orientation}
    43	
    44	Thus high-side conversion conjugates an arbitrary complex modulation. This is
    45	not merely a minus sign attached to one test tone. For $a(t)=A e^{j2\pi\nu t}$,
    46	the high-side IF is centered at $f_L-f_R$ with offset $-\nu$ and envelope phase
    47	$-\arg A+\lambda$. For a phase-modulated waveform, every instantaneous modulation
    48	phase changes sign. For amplitude modulation with a real envelope, that inversion
    49	can be hidden by the test waveform.
    50	
    51	[Analog Devices MT-080, Rev. 0, pp. 1–3](https://www.analog.com/media/en/training-seminars/tutorials/MT-080.pdf)
    52	introduces sum/difference products and distinguishes high/low-side injection.
    53	Its ideal multiplier is not a guarantee of practical mixer gain or linearity.
    54	@eq-mixer-orientation is derived here with explicit envelope scaling.
    55	
    56	Our synthetic plan has $f_R=1.000$ GHz, $f_L=1.020$ GHz and positive IF center
    57	$f_I=20$ MHz. After a real IF filter with response $H(f)$, ideal real sampling at
    58	$F_s=100$ MHz and digital mixing by
    59	$e^{-j(\omega_0n+\chi)}$, $\omega_0=2\pi f_I/F_s$, the selected complex band
    60	has the high-side orientation. Conjugating that band once restores the RF
    61	orientation. For a single RF tone offset $\nu$, a physical RF delay $\tau_R$
    62	and constant LO/NCO phases, its main-path complex amplitude at output is
    63	
    64	$$
    65	Z(\nu)=A e^{-j2\pi(f_R+\nu)\tau_R}
    66	 H^*(f_I-\nu)e^{-j\lambda+j\chi}.
    67	$$ {#eq-restored-transfer}
    68	
    69	Here $A$ is the RF-plane peak phasor; any real positive scalar conversion gain
    70	has been factored out. The IF filter precedes sampling. In the worked digital FIR
    71	below, $H$ is instead its discrete-time steady response evaluated at analog
    72	frequency modulo $F_s$; this substitution is valid only for the declared ideal
    73	sampled path. Finite real-image terms are retained separately, rather than
    74	silently included in a scalar $H$.
    75	
    76	![Follow the waveform as well as its center frequency. The main-band drawing omits real mirror leakage; the finite-record equation below restores it. Scalar gain is factored out.](figures/frequency-transfer-orientation.svg){#fig-frequency-transfer-orientation fig-alt="Envelope path showing high-side conjugation, real sampling, FIR response, digital mixing and the final conjugation that restores RF orientation. LO and NCO phases enter at different planes."}
    77	
    78	The reference sensitivity follows directly. A positive LO phase perturbation
    79	appears as a **negative** restored output phase perturbation. If the LO source
    80	phase is $\lambda_s$ and its distribution delay is $\tau_L$, then
    81	$\lambda=\lambda_s-2\pi f_L\tau_L$. Allowing an NCO phase perturbation,
    82	
    83	$$
    84	\delta\phi_i=-2\pi f_R\delta\tau_{R,i}
    85	 +2\pi f_L\delta\tau_{L,i}-\delta\lambda_s+\delta\chi_i
    86	$$ {#eq-transfer-path-sensitivity}
    87	
    88	at the center RF tone; set $\delta\chi_i=0$ when the NCO state is held fixed. Common $\lambda_s$ cancels in an ideal simultaneous
    89	relative comparison; unequal endpoint delays and their changes do not. Frequency
    90	conversion does not convert every physical delay into an IF-frequency phase
    91	error. The RF path is weighted by RF frequency and the LO path by LO frequency.
    92	
    93	Reference multiplication and division also carry phase. For an ideal harmonic
    94	multiplier of integer order $M$, a chosen harmonic has phase
    95	$M\phi+\phi_{M,0}$, including its additive phase error. An ideal divide-by-$N$
    96	output satisfies $N\theta=\phi$ modulo $2\pi$, so
    97	
    98	$$
    99	\theta=\frac{\phi}{N}+\frac{2\pi q}{N},\qquad q\in\{0,\ldots,N-1\}.
   100	$$
   101	
   102	The integer $q$ is an edge/state choice, not small noise. For centered small phase
   103	fluctuations within one known state, multiplication/division scales phase PSD by
   104	$M^2$ or $N^{-2}$ before additive disturbances; the offset-frequency variable is
   105	unchanged in this ideal phase-process model. This statement supplies neither a
   106	PLL transfer function nor deterministic divider initialization. A frequency
   107	relation alone leaves $q$ undetermined.

   109	## Bands and unwanted responses {#sec-frequency-exclusions}
   110	
   111	Before making a scalar transfer claim, list every physical path that reaches the
   112	observed band. For real sampling,
   113	$e^{j2\pi(f+kF_s)n/F_s}=e^{j2\pi fn/F_s}$ for integer $k$.
   114	The principal signed alias is $f_a=f-F_s\lfloor f/F_s+1/2\rfloor$ in
   115	$[-F_s/2,F_s/2)$. A real waveform also contains the negative-frequency conjugate.
   116	Folding to a positive plotted frequency therefore needs an additional orientation
   117	check. This algebra, rather than a mnemonic about Nyquist zones, determines the
   118	sign for an asymmetric modulation.
   119	
   120	[MT-002, Rev. A, pp. 9–11](https://www.analog.com/media/en/training-seminars/tutorials/MT-002.pdf)
   121	discusses zone inversion and analog filtering. Here alias placement is derived
   122	for an ideal sampler; aperture response, converter noise and distortion remain
   123	separate implementation inputs.
   124	
   125	For the plan above, consider a receiver passband of $\pm100$ kHz around the wanted
   126	carrier; the architecture's worked signal itself is a tone. The same digital band
   127	receives an RF image at $1.040$ GHz through the 20 MHz IF. A signal near 1.100 GHz
   128	produces an 80 MHz IF whose real sampled image lies at 20 MHz. The IF response
   129	must be evaluated at **80 MHz before sampling**, not 20 MHz after folding. Once
   130	these analog paths overlap in the samples, a downstream linear filter cannot
   131	separate arbitrary independent waveforms with identical sampled support.

   135	A first spur inventory should likewise propagate candidate products
   136	$|m f_R\pm n f_L|$ through the sampler and digital selection. For example,
   137	$2f_L-2f_R=40$ MHz lies outside a 20 MHz IF passband, but other residual products overlap after sampling:
   138	
   139	| Residual analog product at the sampler | Frequency | Principal sampled alias | Consequence |
   140	|---|---:|---:|---|
   141	| RF + LO sum product | 2020 MHz | +20 MHz | Overlaps wanted; IF sum rejection required |
   142	| LO feedthrough | 1020 MHz | +20 MHz | Overlaps wanted; isolation/IF rejection required |
   143	| $2f_R-f_L$ nonlinear product | 980 MHz | −20 MHz | Real conjugate also overlaps; amplitude needs nonlinear evidence |

   145	Frequencies here are at nominal centers; propagate each product's actual
   146	sideband offsets and conjugations before accepting a modulation plan.
   147	The finite inventory $|m|,|n|\le2$ is a useful first check, not an
   148	exhaustive nonlinear model. Product amplitudes require part-specific drive,
   149	loading, compression, isolation and multi-signal evidence; integer labels do not

   153	### A finite observation that can be exercised
   154	
   155	The architecture requires composite blocker-to-record voltage transfer no larger
   156	than $\eta_B=10^{-5}$, normalized to the wanted main response. Merely selecting
   157	10 MHz for a blocker and 20 MHz for the wanted IF does not establish this.
   158	At a noninteger record offset, a rectangular record leaks both real images.
   159	
   160	As a reproducible **operator candidate**, use a real three-tap FIR before digital
   161	mixing:
   162	
   163	$$
   164	h=[1,-2\cos(0.2\pi),1],\quad
   165	H(f)=e^{-j\omega}[2\cos\omega-2\cos(0.2\pi)],\quad
   166	\omega=2\pi f/F_s.
   167	$$ {#eq-three-tap-notch}
   168	
   169	It has a notch at 10 MHz and unit magnitude at 20 MHz. The latter response is
   170	$e^{j108^\circ}$, with group delay one sample in its nonzero, constant-sign band.
   171	The FIR needs two genuine preceding samples; discarding two initial outputs or
   172	supplying valid continuous history is part of the observation definition.
   173	
   174	Define the normalized record sum, for $N=100000$ samples, $T=N/F_s=1$ ms,
   175	
   176	$$
   177	D_N(f)=\frac1N\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}e^{j2\pi fn/F_s}
   178	 =e^{j\pi(N-1)f/F_s}\frac{\sin(\pi Nf/F_s)}{N\sin(\pi f/F_s)}.
   179	$$
   180	
   181	At integer multiples of $F_s$, use the continuous limit 1. A real tone with
   182	positive-frequency peak phasor $B$ after conversion but before this FIR gives,
   183	**before final conjugation**,
   184	
   185	$$
   186	Y=e^{-j\chi}\{B H(f)D_N(f-f_I)
   187	 +B^* H^*(f)D_N(-f-f_I)\}.
   188	$$ {#eq-real-record}
   189	
   190	This follows by substituting $x[n]=(B e^{j2\pi fn/F_s}+B^*e^{-j2\pi fn/F_s})/2$
   191	into $2N^{-1}\sum(h*x)[n]e^{-j(\omega_0n+\chi)}$.
   192	No random phase or favorable cancellation was assumed. Final $Z=Y^*$.
   193	The second term explains why the exact finite real observation is generally a
   194	map in both $B$ and $B^*$, rather than a complex scalar gain alone.
   195	
   196	For wanted and blocker RF offsets each in $[-100,100]$ Hz, put
   197	$f_w=20\text{ MHz}-\delta_w$ and $f_b=10\text{ MHz}-\delta_b$.
   198	At the worst offset, $|H(f_b)|\le7.387\times10^{-6}$. If the middle coefficient
   199	has error $|\epsilon_c|\le10^{-6}$, its additional response has magnitude at
   200	most $10^{-6}$. Meanwhile the two blocker sums obey
   201	
   202	$$
   203	|D_N(f_b-f_I)|+|D_N(-f_b-f_I)|<1.383\times10^{-5}.
   204	$$
   205	
   206	To check this bound without a sweep, each numerator is at most $\sin(0.1\pi)$;
   207	the two denominator sine magnitudes are at least
   208	$\sin[\pi(0.1-10^{-6})]$ and $\sin[\pi(0.3-10^{-6})]$, respectively.
   209	The wanted main coefficient is greater than 0.9836 including this coefficient
   210	error. Thus the **sum** of blocker-path magnitudes relative to that main path is
   211	less than $1.3\times10^{-10}$ in this steady, exact-arithmetic model, comfortably
   212	below the supplied $10^{-5}$ interface. The wanted mirror/main ratio is bounded
   213	by $3.4\times10^{-6}$; it is a separate signal-dependent error, not blocker
   214	rejection. Its per-channel phase magnitude is at most $\arcsin(3.4\times10^{-6})$,
   215	about $0.000195^\circ$, and it must be charged if retained.
   216	
   217	![The center null alone proves little. Offset bounds, coefficient error, both real images and the finite observation produce the stated rejection envelope. The plotted exact center is clipped at −130 dB for display; its mathematical value is zero.](figures/notch-observation.svg){#fig-notch-observation fig-alt="Notch magnitude versus a small blocker frequency offset, showing the exact coefficient and a coefficient-error envelope, followed by the finite-observation rejection conditions."}
   218	
   219	This example provides an executable transfer, not a selected filter or deployed
   220	rejection guarantee. It omits arithmetic roundoff/overflow, reset transients,
   221	additional analog aliases/spurs and clock error. The FIR changes noise transfer;
   222	the architecture's effective $N_0$ must refer to this complete observation or be
   223	recomputed from source spectra. It cannot simply be copied from a different
   224	filter. Two delays and one constant multiply per input sample imply roughly
   225	300 million constant multiplies/s for three 100 MS/s channels before any
   226	optimization, plus the digital mixer/accumulation. Symmetry and fixed coefficients
   227	may reduce cost; no implementation/power claim follows. The two-sample history
   228	adds 20 ns of startup data, distinct from the FIR's 10 ns group delay and from
   229	processing/transport latency. Those distinctions matter to the 0.6 ms processing
   230	and 2.5 W envelopes in Chapter 12.

   232	## Response over bandwidth {#sec-transfer-bandwidth}
   233	
   234	Take the worked input tone phase $25^\circ$, RF delay $\tau_R=25$ ps,
   235	LO phase $\lambda=17^\circ$ at L and NCO phase $\chi=11^\circ$ at the defined
   236	sample origin. @eq-restored-transfer gives at the carrier
   237	
   238	$$
   239	\phi_Z=25^\circ-9^\circ-17^\circ-108^\circ+11^\circ=-98^\circ.
   240	$$
   241	
   242	For an RF sideband at $\nu=+50$ kHz, the IF is 19.95 MHz. Its FIR phase is
   243	$108.18^\circ$, while the RF delay contributes $-9.00045^\circ$.
   244	The restored tone therefore has offset **+50 kHz** and phase
   245	$-98.18045^\circ$ at the declared origin. This is the sideband's waveform
   246	phasor, not the output of a center-frequency 1 ms accumulation: that record has
   247	a null at 50 kHz. Extracting this tone requires following its frequency, as in
   248	the waveform check, or inspecting the complex waveform before accumulation. An independent real-waveform
   249	mix/filter/sample calculation tests this result; an amplitude-only test cannot
   250	show its orientation.
   251	
   252	For a smooth nonzero main transfer $G(\nu)$, define equivalent envelope group
   253	delay as $\tau_g=-[2\pi]^{-1}d\arg G/d\nu$. Because
   254	$G(\nu)=e^{-j2\pi(f_R+\nu)\tau_R}H^*(f_I-\nu)$ up to constant reference phases,
   255	the two reversals give
   256	
   257	$$
   258	\tau_g(\nu)=\tau_R+\tau_{g,H}(f_I-\nu).
   259	$$
   260	
   261	For this FIR, it is $10.025$ ns. The carrier phase intercept is **not**
   262	$-2\pi f_R\tau_g$: the RF carrier and IF filter use different frequency origins.
   263	A single-tone calibration removes an intercept but cannot establish the slope.
   264	A differential slope $\Delta\tau$ produces phase error
   265	$-2\pi\nu\Delta\tau$ after center correction; a $0.1^\circ$ limit at
   266	$|\nu|=100$ kHz requires $|\Delta\tau|\le2.778$ ns under a pure-delay model.
   267	
   268	Nor does unit magnitude imply undistorted modulation. Consider a further
   269	orientation-restored equivalent all-pass response
   270	$Q(\nu)=(1-j\nu/f_p)/(1+j\nu/f_p)$, $f_p=100$ kHz. It has magnitude 1,
   271	phase $-2\arctan(\nu/f_p)$ and delay
   272	$1/[\pi f_p(1+(\nu/f_p)^2)]$. At 50 kHz its phase is $-53.130^\circ$,
   273	whereas extrapolating its center delay predicts $-57.296^\circ$.
   274	The $4.166^\circ$ discrepancy affects relative sideband timing and waveform shape.
   275	This is a stable causal first-order all-pass in the equivalent complex path,
   276	not a specified RF component. A sweep or known asymmetric modulation is needed
   277	to assess dispersion; a flat level response and a center phase correction miss it.
   278	Even two chosen tones can conceal curvature. For this $Q$, the values at
   279	$\nu=\pm50$ kHz exactly match a pure delay of 2.951672353 microseconds; both
   280	responses also equal one at the center. Their phases differ by 16.260205° at
   281	+100 kHz. Sweep the tone locations, use additional suitably placed frequencies,
   282	or compare against an independently established delay. A fixed tone pair alone
   283	identifies a secant slope and phase intercept, not general phase curvature.
   284

Synthetic exact transfer curves illustrate why equal carrier phase and equal magnitude do not ensure equal modulation transfer.](figures/transfer-response.svg){#fig-transfer-response fig-alt="Two plots compare orientation-restored phase and group delay of the basic RF/FIR path with the same path plus a unity-magnitude all-pass.    287	## State-sensitive plans {#sec-transfer-states}
   288	
   289	A plan has state coordinates as well as frequencies. In this example record the
   290	LO/divider state, actual sample origin, NCO accumulator phase, filter history and
   291	calibration reference planes. A positive one-sample shift means that sample
   292	label $n$ now contains the old waveform at $n+1$ while the NCO label remains $n$.
   293	Before restoration that advances a 20 MHz IF by $72^\circ$; after conjugation it
   294	changes output phase by **−72°**. If the NCO/sample labels shift consistently,
   295	the result differs: specify what moved before correcting it. A +90° NCO phase
   296	change gives +90° restored phase. A divide-by-2 reference state change can give
   297	180° LO change, hence −180° output change. Equal output frequencies in all three
   298	cases do not imply a valid comparison to the prior calibration.
   299	
   300	Actual hardware documentation makes these conditions concrete.
   301	[AD9208 Rev. 0, p. 49 and pp. 78–81](https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD9208.pdf)
   302	separately describes NCO-accumulator synchronization, link latency, SYSREF timing
   303	and multichip alignment. Its p. 49 SPI reset method is limited to NCOs on one
   304	chip; the SYSREF method has enabling conditions. Page 78 requires distribution
   305	skew, setup/hold and link-latency conditions. This is evidence of conditional
   306	state mechanisms in that device/revision, not evidence that our synthetic
   307	100 MS/s plan uses it or has deterministic RF phase. The p. 80 timestamp-mode
   308	paragraph also contains apparently conflicting reset wording; no reset guarantee
   309	is imported from it. Consult the relevant revision and implementation evidence
   310	before depending on a mode.
   311	
   312	Calibration should exercise what the measurement needs. A known RF phase change
   313	at plane R tests conversion orientation; a positive frequency-offset change tests
   314	modulation orientation and slope. A coherent RF sweep can identify differential
   315	transfer over the usable band. Injection after an RF selector cannot identify
   316	its phase, and no electronic injection establishes the antenna's field response.
   317	A restart test must retain sample identity and reference/NCO state evidence, and
   318	must distinguish constant offsets from invalid or settling records. These are
   319	verification implications of the transfer, not a complete transition procedure.
   320	
   321	To transfer the method, lower the LO to 980 MHz while keeping a positive 20 MHz
   322	IF. Derive the low-side selected envelope and the NCO sign; determine whether the
   323	final conjugation should remain. Trace the RF image at 960 MHz and a +50 kHz
   324	wanted sideband. The low-side envelope is $a e^{-j\lambda}$, so ordinary negative
   325	20 MHz digital mixing already restores the wanted orientation; retaining the
   326	conjugation would reverse it. The wanted IF sideband is +50 kHz and the 960 MHz
   327	image sideband is inverted. Finally, suppose only a center-tone calibration is
   328	available and the extra all-pass is possible: the data cannot establish the
   329	2.778 ns differential-delay envelope. The engineering choice stays conditional
   330	until bandwidth-sensitive evidence or a justified physical bound is supplied.

## Reciprocal mixing: a blocker makes LO noise observable {#sec-reciprocal-mixing}

Use a separate power-normalized envelope $b(t)$, in $\sqrt{\rm W}$, for the blocker
after RF preselection, referred to a stated mixer input impedance. Its mean power
is $P_B=E|b|^2$. For a peak voltage across a real resistance $R_0$, this envelope
is $b=z/\sqrt{2R_0}$. With RF amplitude transfer $F$ in these fixed
power-normalized coordinates, $S_b(\nu)=|F(\nu)|^2S_{b_{\rm RF}}(\nu)$.
Thus 20 dB power attenuation means $|F|^2=0.01$, not an amplitude factor of 0.01.
Let the ideal conversion have unit power gain and common
spectral orientation. A small effective LO phase $\phi_{\rm eff}$ gives

$$
 b(t)e^{-j\phi_{\rm eff}(t)}
 \simeq b(t)-jb(t)\phi_{\rm eff}(t).
$$

The product term moves LO phase fluctuations onto the blocker. For a centered
stationary LO phase independent of a centered stationary blocker, its covariance factors
into blocker correlation times phase correlation. Fourier transformation gives
the convolution

$$
 S_{\rm rm}(f)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
 S_b(\nu)S_{\phi,\rm eff}(f-\nu)\,d\nu,
 \qquad
 P_{\rm rm}=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|W(f)|^2S_{\rm rm}(f)\,df.
$$

Here $f,\nu$ are offsets from the wanted converted carrier, $W$ is the subsequent
observation transfer, $S_b$ is in W/Hz and $S_{\phi,\rm eff}$ is the two-sided
real-phase PSD in rad²/Hz. Finite supports or convergent integrals are required.
Deterministic narrow blockers can be treated directly as tones, or by a uniform
random initial phase for the stationary correlation derivation. A tone at offset
$\Delta$ gives $S_{\rm rm}(f)=P_BS_{\phi,\rm eff}(f-\Delta)$. If that density
is flat over the observation band, $P_{\rm rm}=P_BS_{\phi,\rm eff}(-\Delta)B_W$,
where $B_W=\int|W(f)|^2df$ Hz. This is a derived narrow-blocker/flat-spectrum limit,
not an assumption that all blockers or phase spectra are white.

The effective phase can include source/distribution phase plus noise created
after an accessible LO filter:
$\phi_{\rm eff}=H_0*\phi_0+\sum_r H_r*\eta_r$. The star here denotes filtering.
For independent branch sources its density is
$|H_0|^2S_{\phi_0}+\sum_r|H_r|^2S_{\eta_r}$; correlated branches require the full
cross-spectral sum. Analog Devices' [mixer-noise article](https://www.analog.com/en/resources/technical-articles/specifications-and-measurement-of-local-oscillator-noise-in-integrated-circuit-base-station-mixers.html),
“Mixer Noise Model” and “Effective Noise Floor of LO Driver,” explains the blocker
mechanism and internal LO-driver contributions. Its equation images are not used
to set our normalization or device values. The relationships here follow from
the specified envelope multiplication. A source-connector phase-noise test alone
cannot establish the effective internal spectrum.

"""Distinct physical/numerical formulations for bounded system examples."""
import unittest,math,cmath,sys,random
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path(__file__).parents[1]/'engineering/examples'))
import system_models as model


class RequirementModels(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_peak_voltage_against_phase_swept_real_waveforms(self):
        for attenuation,loss in [(0,0),(30,2),(40,2),(60,2)]:
            lo,hi=model.gain_bounds(attenuation,loss)
            ps=1e-3*10**((-100-loss)/10);pb=1e-3*10**((-20-attenuation)/10)
            a=math.sqrt(100*ps);b=math.sqrt(100*pb)
            # Commensurate tones reach their worst joint peak at t=0.
            peak=max(abs(a*math.cos(2*math.pi*.7*t/10000)+b*math.cos(2*math.pi*1.3*t/10000)) for t in range(10001))
            self.assertAlmostEqual(peak*10**(hi/20),.1,places=13)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(a*10**(lo/20),math.sqrt(100e-9),places=13)
        self.assertGreater(*model.gain_bounds(0,0))
        self.assertLess(*model.gain_bounds(40,2))

    def test_spatial_aliases_and_local_finite_difference(self):
        k=2*math.pi/.3
        self.assertAlmostEqual(abs(cmath.exp(1j*k*1.2*.25)-cmath.exp(1j*k*1.2*.5)),0,places=13)
        self.assertGreater(abs(cmath.exp(1j*k*.15*.25)-cmath.exp(1j*k*.15*.5)),.7)
        th=math.pi/3;eps=1e-6
        derivative=(k*1.2*math.sin(th+eps)-k*1.2*math.sin(th-eps))/(2*eps)
        sigma=math.degrees(1/derivative/math.sqrt(100))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(sigma,.45594532639052,places=8)
        low,high=model.aperture_limits();self.assertGreater(low,high)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(cmath.exp(1j*k*high*math.sin(th)),cmath.exp(-1j*k*high*math.sin(th)),places=12)

    def test_finite_tone_observation_against_midpoint_integration(self):
        n=20000;T=.001;df=100
        average=sum(cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*df*(i+.5)*T/n) for i in range(n))/n
        self.assertAlmostEqual(abs(average)**2*100,model.requirement_case()['rho'],places=7)
        needed=model.requirement_case()['short_rho'];self.assertGreater(needed/1e5,.0025)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(needed,5321.885200828357,places=8)

    def test_branch_error_covariance_from_three_physical_noise_sources(self):
        rng=random.Random(1113);k=2*math.pi/.3;rho=model.requirement_case()['rho']
        a,b=1/(k*.15),1/(k*1.2);sd=1/math.sqrt(2*rho);n=100000
        moments=0.
        for _ in range(n):
            e0,es,el=[rng.gauss(0,sd) for _ in range(3)]
            error=a*(es-e0)-b*(el-e0);moments+=error**2
        theoretical=(a*a+b*b-a*b)/rho
        self.assertLess(abs(moments/n/theoretical-1),.018)
        self.assertLess(model.requirement_case()['branch_sum'],1e-3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(3*14*100e6*1.1,4.62e9,places=4)
        self.assertGreater(3*14*100e6*1.25,5e9)

    def test_retained_blocker_disk_and_composite_contract(self):
        q=model.retained_blocker();r=q['r'];phases=[2*math.pi*i/20000 for i in range(20001)]
        maximum=max(abs(cmath.phase(1+r*cmath.exp(1j*p))) for p in phases)
        minimum=min(abs(1+r*cmath.exp(1j*p)) for p in phases)
        self.assertLess(abs(maximum-q['beta']),1e-10)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(minimum,1-r,places=14)
        self.assertLess(q['branch_bound'],1e-3)
        # Exact inverse manifold, rather than a linear angular conversion.
        perturbed=math.asin(math.sin(math.pi/3)+2*q['beta']/(8*math.pi))
        self.assertLess(math.degrees(perturbed-math.pi/3),.02)
        amplitude_leak=10**(42/20)*abs(math.sin(math.pi*100.5)/(math.pi*100.5))
        self.assertGreater(amplitude_leak,.39)
        self.assertLess(q['minimum_rho'],model.requirement_case()['rho'])

    def test_reference_endpoint_allowances_by_complex_tones(self):
        tau=.05/(360*1.02e9)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(math.degrees(abs(cmath.phase(cmath.exp(-2j*math.pi*1.02e9*tau)))),.05,places=13)
        df=.05/(360*.001)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(math.degrees(cmath.phase(cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*df*.001))),.05,places=13)
        eps=.05/(360*20e6*.001)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(math.degrees(cmath.phase(cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*20e6*eps*.001))),.05,places=13)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(math.degrees(cmath.phase(cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*20e6/100e6))),72.,places=12)
        required=sum([1e-3/10**(-6/10)]*3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(required,.011943215116604916,places=14)

    def test_phase_uncertainty_against_complex_voltage_noise(self):
        rng=random.Random(321);rho=model.requirement_case()['rho'];sd=1/math.sqrt(2*rho)
        n=60000;variance=0.
        for _ in range(n):
            x=1+complex(rng.gauss(0,sd),rng.gauss(0,sd))
            y=1+complex(rng.gauss(0,sd),rng.gauss(0,sd))
            variance+=cmath.phase(y*x.conjugate())**2
        # Checks the local approximation at the supplied SNR, not rare-event tails.
        self.assertLess(abs(variance/n*rho-1),.025)


class TransferModels(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_real_mixer_band_selection_and_sampled_waveform(self):
        # Independent real RF/LO multiplication at 5 GS/s, ideal analog IF mask,
        # then decimation, periodic steady FIR history and real-record extraction.
        import numpy as np
        fs=5e9;n=100000;t=np.arange(n)/fs
        for nu in [0,50000,-50000]:
            rf=np.cos(2*np.pi*(1e9+nu)*(t-25e-12)+math.radians(25))
            lo=2*np.cos(2*np.pi*1.02e9*t+math.radians(17))
            ff=np.fft.fftfreq(n,1/fs);spectrum=np.fft.fft(rf*lo)
            spectrum[np.abs(np.abs(ff)-20e6)>100001]=0
            x=np.fft.ifft(spectrum).real[::50]
            h=x-1.618033988749895*np.roll(x,1)+np.roll(x,2)
            # Extract the offset tone, using its actual digital frequency.
            ref=np.exp(-1j*(2*np.pi*(20e6-nu)*np.arange(len(x))/100e6+math.radians(11)))
            result=(2*np.mean(h*ref)).conjugate()
            self.assertAlmostEqual(abs(result),abs(model.notch_response(20e6-nu)),places=10)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(cmath.phase(result),model.transfer_phase(nu),places=10)

    def test_exact_real_record_and_offset_rejection(self):
        n=100000;f=10e6-100;fs=100e6;b=cmath.exp(.7j)
        # Direct samples with valid prehistory, versus geometric-path law.
        coef=-2*math.cos(.2*math.pi)
        x=lambda k:(b*cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*f*k/fs)).real
        actual=2*sum((x(k)+coef*x(k-1)+x(k-2))*cmath.exp(-2j*math.pi*.2*k) for k in range(n))/n
        paths=model.observation_paths(f)
        expected=b*paths[0]+b.conjugate()*paths[1]
        self.assertLess(abs(actual-expected),2e-13)
        for dw in [-100,-57,0,38,100]:
            for db in [-100,-71,0,42,100]:
                for error in [-1e-6,0,1e-6]:
                    self.assertLess(model.composite_notch_rejection(dw,db,coef+error),1.3e-10)

    def test_phase_slope_allpass_and_state_changes(self):
        eps=100
        delay=-(model.transfer_phase(eps)-model.transfer_phase(-eps))/(4*math.pi*eps)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(delay,10.025e-9,places=16)
        q=lambda v:(1-1j*v/1e5)/(1+1j*v/1e5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(abs(q(50000)),1.,places=14)
        fitted_delay=-cmath.phase(q(50000))/(2*math.pi*50000)
        for f in [-50000,0,50000]:
            self.assertAlmostEqual(q(f),cmath.exp(-2j*math.pi*f*fitted_delay),places=13)
        self.assertGreater(abs(math.degrees(cmath.phase(q(100000)*cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*100000*fitted_delay)))),16.)
        self.assertGreater(abs(math.degrees(cmath.phase(q(50000)))+360*50000/(math.pi*1e5)),4)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(math.degrees(cmath.phase(cmath.exp(-2j*math.pi*.2))),-72.)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(model.transfer_phase(nco_phase=math.radians(101))-model.transfer_phase(),math.pi/2)

    def test_real_alias_identity_and_lost_discrimination(self):
        for n in range(37):
            self.assertAlmostEqual(math.cos(2*math.pi*80.05e6*n/100e6+.3),math.cos(2*math.pi*19.95e6*n/100e6-.3),places=12)


class AllocationModels(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_nonzero_offset_phase_weight_and_persistent_departure(self):
        T=.002;df=100;n=20000;step=T/n;eps=1e-5
        times=[-T/2+(i+.5)*step for i in range(n)]
        psi=[math.cos(2*math.pi*250*t) for t in times]
        baseline=sum(cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*df*t) for t in times)/n
        actual=cmath.phase(sum(cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*df*t+1j*eps*p) for t,p in zip(times,psi))/n/baseline)/eps
        weight=[math.cos(2*math.pi*df*t)/(T*model.sinc(df*T)) for t in times]
        predicted=sum(g*p for g,p in zip(weight,psi))*step
        self.assertAlmostEqual(actual,predicted,places=8)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(sum(weight)*step,1.,places=9)
        # A constant departure passes with unit sensitivity, not 1/sqrt(N).
        constant=cmath.phase(baseline*cmath.exp(.01j)/baseline)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(constant,.01,places=14)

    def test_thermal_signs_by_physical_complex_paths(self):
        hu,hv=model.thermal_paths();step=.001
        for i,(rf,lo) in enumerate([(1.5e-12,.5e-12),(3e-12,4e-12)]):
            transfer=lambda u,v:cmath.exp(-2j*math.pi*1e9*rf*(u+v))*cmath.exp(2j*math.pi*1.02e9*lo*u)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(cmath.phase(transfer(step,0))/step,hu[i],places=13)
            self.assertAlmostEqual(cmath.phase(transfer(0,step))/step,hv[i],places=13)
        # Independent temperatures would delete a consequential cross term.
        wrong=4*((2*math.pi*1.02e9*4e-12)**2+(2*math.pi*1e9*3e-12)**2)
        self.assertGreater(wrong/(4*hu[1]**2),21)

    def test_covariance_from_common_complex_voltage_and_slow_sources(self):
        import numpy as np
        rng=np.random.default_rng(130013);n=240000;q=.02;rho=100*model.sinc(.1)**2
        cn=lambda shape:(rng.normal(size=shape)+1j*rng.normal(size=shape))/math.sqrt(2)
        data=model.nominal_allocation();v=np.array(data['v']);hu,hv=map(np.array,model.thermal_paths())
        u=rng.normal(0,2,n);grad=rng.normal(0,1.8,n);cal=rng.normal(0,.01,(n,3))
        phases=((math.sqrt(1-q)*cn((n,3))+math.sqrt(q)*cn((n,1))*v)/math.sqrt(rho)).imag+cal
        dif=phases[:,1:]-phases[:,:1]+u[:,None]*hu+grad[:,None]*hv
        measured=np.cov(dif,rowvar=False,bias=True);expected=np.array(data['covariance'])
        self.assertLess(np.max(np.abs(measured-expected)),9e-5)
        ub=(math.sin(math.pi/3)-.125)/1.01
        self.assertAlmostEqual(cmath.phase(v[1]),-math.pi/8,places=12)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(abs(cmath.phase(v[2])),math.pi,places=12)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(math.sin(math.radians(47.19651350605626)),ub,places=13)
        self.assertGreater(data['sigma_degrees'],.5)
        self.assertLess(model.nominal_allocation(q=0)['sigma_degrees'],.5)

    def test_source_row_envelope_with_bounded_mean_changes(self):
        rng=random.Random(13013);q=.02;rho=100*model.sinc(.1)**2;case=model.allocation_case();r=case['r']
        for _ in range(400):
            w=[rng.uniform(-1,1) for i in range(3)]
            v=[cmath.exp(1j*rng.uniform(-math.pi,math.pi)) for i in range(3)]
            means=[1+r*cmath.exp(1j*rng.uniform(-math.pi,math.pi)) for i in range(3)]
            # Phase derivative divides the proper complex source by its mean.
            actual=((1-q)*sum((a/abs(z))**2 for a,z in zip(w,means))+q*abs(sum(a*b/z for a,b,z in zip(w,v,means)))**2)/(2*rho)
            upper=((1-q)*sum(a*a for a in w)+q*sum(abs(a) for a in w)**2)/(2*case['rho_min'])
            self.assertLessEqual(actual,upper*(1+1e-13))

    def test_restoration_and_changed_record_observation(self):
        one=model.allocation_case();two=model.allocation_case(T=.002)
        self.assertGreater(one['sigma_degrees'],.5);self.assertLess(two['sigma_degrees'],.4)
        self.assertLess(two['approx_branch_envelope'],1e-3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(one['gradient_variance'],two['gradient_variance'],places=15)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(one['calibration_variance'],two['calibration_variance'],places=15)
        self.assertLess(model.allocation_case(T=.002,q=.2)['sigma_degrees'],.5)
        for dw in [-100,0,100]:
            for db in [-100,-37,0,59,100]:
                for err in [-1e-6,1e-6]:
                    self.assertLess(model.composite_notch_rejection(dw,db,-2*math.cos(.2*math.pi)+err,samples=200000),1.3e-10)
        # Finite-SNR sensitivity is separate from an assumed new source.
        inflated=one['total_phase_variance']+.01*one['noise_phase_variance']
        self.assertGreater(inflated,one['allowed_variance'])

def gain_bounds(blocker_attenuation=40,wanted_loss=2):
    """dB bounds at equal50ohm planes; two-tone worst composite voltage."""
    ps=10**((-100-wanted_loss)/10)
    pb=10**((-20-blocker_attenuation)/10)
    return 40+wanted_loss,-10-20*log10(sqrt(ps)+sqrt(pb))


def aperture_limits(rho=100):
    k=2*pi/.3
    return 1/(k*.5*radians(.5)*sqrt(rho)),.3/(2*sin(pi/3))


def requirement_case():
    k=2*pi/.3;ds=.15;dl=1.2;rho=100*sinc(.1)**2
    variance=(1/(k*ds)**2+1/(k*dl)**2-1/(k*ds*k*dl))/rho
    nd=NormalDist();m=pi-k*ds*sin(pi/3)
    terms=(2*nd.cdf(-.3/(2*dl)/sqrt(variance)),2*nd.cdf(-m*sqrt(rho)))
    return {'rho':rho,'gain_bounds':gain_bounds(),
            'fine_sigma_degrees':degrees(1/(k*dl*.5*sqrt(rho))),
            'branch_terms':terms,'branch_sum':sum(terms),
            'short_rho':1/(k*ds*.5*radians(.5))**2}


def retained_blocker(eta=1e-5):
    """Composite path-magnitude contract; high-SNR phase approximation."""
    from math import asin
    k=2*pi/.3;rho=requirement_case()['rho'];r=10**(42/20)*eta
    beta=asin(r);minimum_rho=rho*(1-r)**2
    a,b=1/(k*.15),1/(k*1.2)
    sd=sqrt((a*a+b*b-a*b)/minimum_rho)
    bu=2*beta*(a+b);m=pi-k*.15*sin(pi/3)
    nd=NormalDist()
    return {'r':r,'beta':beta,'minimum_rho':minimum_rho,
            'local_sigma_degrees':degrees(1/(k*1.2*.5*sqrt(minimum_rho))),
            'local_bias_degrees':degrees(2*beta/(k*1.2*.5)),
            'branch_bound':2*nd.cdf(-(.125-bu)/sd)+2*nd.cdf(-(m-2*beta)*sqrt(minimum_rho))}

def thermal_paths():
    """Relative RF/LO delay sensitivities, synthetic ps/K translated to rad/K."""
    lo=[.5e-12,4e-12];rf=[1.5e-12,3e-12]
    return ([2*pi*(1.02e9*l-1e9*r) for l,r in zip(lo,rf)],[-2*pi*1e9*r for r in rf])


def allocation_case(T=.001,sigma_gradient=2,q=.02):
    """Linear Gaussian phase envelope; no physical validation or tail guarantee."""
    from math import asin
    k=2*pi/.3;a,b=1/(k*.15),1/(k*1.2)
    r=10**(42/20)*1e-5+3.4e-6;beta=asin(r)
    rho=1e5*T*sinc(100*T)**2*(1-r)**2
    hu,hv=thermal_paths();noise=(1+q)/rho;cal=.0002;ambient=4*hu[1]**2
    gradient=sigma_gradient**2*hv[1]**2
    total=noise+cal+ambient+gradient
    allowed=(k*1.2*.5*radians(.5))**2
    remaining=allowed-noise-cal-ambient
    gradient_limit=sqrt(remaining)/abs(hv[1]) if remaining>=0 else float('nan')
    evar=((1-q)*(a*a+b*b-a*b)+2*q*a*a)/rho
    evar+=1e-4*((b-a)**2+a*a+b*b)+4*(a*hu[0]-b*hu[1])**2+sigma_gradient**2*(a*hv[0]-b*hv[1])**2
    svar=noise+cal+4*hu[0]**2+sigma_gradient**2*hv[0]**2
    m=pi-k*.15*sin(pi/3);bias=2*beta*(a+b);nd=NormalDist()
    branch=2*nd.cdf(-(.125-bias)/sqrt(evar))+2*nd.cdf(-(m-2*beta)/sqrt(svar))
    return {'T':T,'sigma_gradient':sigma_gradient,'q':q,'r':r,'rho_min':rho,
            'noise_phase_variance':noise,'calibration_variance':cal,'ambient_variance':ambient,
            'gradient_variance':gradient,'total_phase_variance':total,'allowed_variance':allowed,
            'sigma_degrees':degrees(sqrt(total)/(k*1.2*.5)),
            'gradient_limit':gradient_limit,'approx_branch_envelope':branch,
            'bias_degrees':degrees(asin(sin(pi/3)+2*beta/(k*1.2))-pi/3)}


def nominal_allocation(theta_blocker=47.19651350605626,sigma_gradient=1.8,q=.02,T=.001):
    """Actual source-root covariance at clean unit means; fixed total density."""
    from cmath import exp
    x=[0,.15,1.2];u=sin(pi/3);ub=sin(radians(theta_blocker))
    v=[exp(2j*pi*xx*(1.01e9*ub-1e9*u)/3e8) for xx in x]
    rho=1e5*T*sinc(100*T)**2
    root=[[((1-q) if i==j else 0)+q*(v[i]*v[j].conjugate()).real for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
    c=[[ (root[i+1][j+1]-root[i+1][0]-root[0][j+1]+root[0][0])/(2*rho) for j in range(2)] for i in range(2)]
    hu,hv=thermal_paths()
    for i in range(2):
        for j in range(2):c[i][j]+=1e-4*(2 if i==j else 1)+4*hu[i]*hu[j]+sigma_gradient**2*hv[i]*hv[j]
    return {'v':v,'covariance':c,'sigma_degrees':degrees(sqrt(c[1][1])/(8*pi*.5))}

def sinc(x): return sin(pi*x)/(pi*x) if x else 1.
def quad(fn,a,b,n=1024):
    h=(b-a)/n
    return h/3*(fn(a)+fn(b)+sum((4 if i%2 else 2)*fn(a+i*h) for i in range(1,n)))

    return 1-x/3+x*x/12-x**3/60 if x<.001 else 2*(x-1+exp(-x))/x**2

I found **no demonstrated consequential mathematical or graphical error in the K13 allocation and revised closure**, under their stated assumptions. The 1 ms failing example and conditional 2 ms restoration are supported by independent calculations. This finding does not establish physical applicability, reader effectiveness, or human acceptance.

All **218 files listed in SHA256SUMS verified**, with no unlisted packet files apart from the manifest itself. I read requirements, relevant accepted scope/CAP-013, manuscript and source passages before examining implementation; consequential calculations preceded author code/tests. Exposure comprised packet requirements and standards, Chapter 12, Chapter 11, relevant prerequisite passages, supplied source notes/anchors, rendered HTML/SVGs, calculation code, tests, and all 21 PNGs. Original source PDFs were unavailable and were not examined. No external sources, connectors, delegation, edits, author conversation, prior reviews or history were used.

The common-source construction withstands the principal challenge. Dividing each blocker’s plane-wave response by its wanted response gives
\(v_i=\exp[j2\pi x_i(f_Bu_B-f_Ru)/c]\).
The stated direction is independently recovered as **47.1965135°**, producing phases \(0,-\pi/8,-\pi\). One proper complex source supplies two shared real quadratures; it is not three independent channel generators. Consequently, the long-comparison variance is \((1-q\cos\psi_l)/\rho\), reaching \((1+q)/\rho\) at this geometry while marginal powers remain fixed. The factor \(1/2\) in Equation 12.3 follows from proper-noise quadrature normalization.

These conclusions require the declared equal relative electronic responses, matched LO-noise transfer and selected-band properness. They do not follow from equal noise powers or identical connector spectra alone. Improper noise requires pseudocovariance as well as covariance; unequal distribution paths require frequency-dependent transfer. [§12.3.1](/tmp/k1113/k13-input/book/feasibility-architecture-allocations.qmd:461) states these restrictions. Holding total density fixed while varying its partition is a legitimate sensitivity experiment, but does not predict what changing a physical blocker or device alone will do.

Chapter 11’s restored transfer gives RF-delay sensitivity \(-2\pi f_R\) and LO-delay sensitivity \(+2\pi f_L\). Applying these independently reproduces
\(h_U=[-0.006220353,+0.006785840]\) and
\(h_V=[-0.009424778,-0.018849556]\) rad/K.
Thus ambient covariance between comparisons is negative, while the RF-only contribution is positive. Summing the two signed ambient paths before squaring gives **0.0001841905 rad²** on the long comparison; incorrectly assigning independent temperatures gives **0.0040499172 rad²**. The cancellation and misleading alternatives are physically and mathematically coherent.

The calibration ensemble is also stated correctly: uncertain intercepts remain fixed between calibrations, and the shared reference contributes to both differences. Neither calibration uncertainty nor record-constant temperature departure acquires independent-sample averaging gain.
